missionPremise: The claim this row was queued under at A-061 -- that a returning browser holds a stale stylesheet across every CSS deploy, blocking the design pass -- was measured with a real Chrome on a persistent profile against the live service in three scenarios and is FALSE (_inbox/2026-08-18_g88_shell_css_cache.md). With no Last-Modified there is no basis for RFC 9111 heuristic freshness, so the browser revalidates, and with no validator that degrades to a full unconditional GET. The real defect is the inverse: sendFile never received req and wrote 200 unconditionally, so a 304 was structurally impossible and every navigation re-transferred every asset. The WDLL therefore re-sequenced item 8 as parallel and explicitly NOT a blocker, and this is a performance and correctness fix.
completionPredicate: All six static routes serve cache-control: no-cache plus a strong per-request content-derived ETag and honour If-None-Match with a bodiless 304; the suite is green with assertions that were each watched failing against the bug they exist to catch; the three HTTP legs pass against a local run of the patched build; a PR is open against main whose check-run conclusion string is success; nothing merged and nothing deployed.
scopeBasis: WDLL item 8 alone. src/server.mjs and src/server.test.mjs only, because two sibling executors hold web/shell.css and src/ui.test.mjs in the same repo concurrently. Filename fingerprinting, a ?v= query param, a build step and no-store were each considered and rejected with reasons in the investigation, and none is revisited here. The deployed-service leg of the WDLL's item 8 check is deliberately NOT claimed: this branch is not deployed, deploys are planner-owned, and code-done is not customer-done.

whatShipped.etagFor: sha256 of the response buffer, base64url, quoted, strong (no W/ prefix). Computed inside the fs.readFile callback on the bytes just read, so it is content-derived on every request by construction.
whatShipped.ifNoneMatchSatisfied: RFC 9110 weak comparison: '*' matches any existing representation, the field is split as a comma list, and a W/ prefix is stripped from both sides before the opaque tags are compared.
whatShipped.sendFile: signature changed from sendFile(res, filePath, contentType) to sendFile(req, res, filePath, contentType). 200 carries content-type + cache-control: no-cache + etag. 304 carries cache-control + etag with no body and deliberately no content-type, per RFC 9110 15.4.5. The 404 branch is unchanged.
whatShipped.whyNoCacheNotNoStore: no-cache means store it but always revalidate: never stale by construction, headers-only when unchanged. no-store is correct for the JSON helper three lines above and wrong here, because it forbids storage entirely and throws away the whole 304 benefit, leaving the re-transfer problem exactly where it was.

bytesPerNavigation.reconciliationFinding: The investigation doc _inbox/2026-08-18_g88_shell_css_cache.md gives app.js 33,214 / shell.css 27,269 / sc-kit.css 4,709 / staff-review.mjs 3,668 and says 'roughly 145 KB'. The dispatch's own table gives 32,914 / 26,969 / 4,409 / 3,368. Every one of those four disagreements is EXACTLY +300 bytes, and index.html agrees exactly at 75,687. Four files off by the same constant is not drift. The figures measured here are byte-identical to the DISPATCH table, taken from a local run at base cdfca39 and again after the patch. Candidate explanations: the investigation counted ~300 B of response headers per asset but took index.html from the file size, or it measured the deployed revision while the detection marker it had appended was still present. NOT RESOLVED HERE -- resolving it needs a measurement against the deployed service, which is the planner's post-merge leg. Use 143,926 with the counting rule above, never 'roughly 145 KB'.

findings.severity: material -- it changes how this item should be graded
findings.title: The third probe leg does NOT catch a constant ETag. Measured, not argued.
findings.claimCorrected: The dispatch and the WDLL item 8 check both state that leg 3, a STALE If-None-Match returning 200 with a full body and a DIFFERENT etag, is 'the one that can fail' and 'a constant or hardcoded etag causes permanent staleness and passes the first two'.
findings.evidence: Negative arm A. With etagFor pinned to a constant, leg 1 still advertises cache-control: no-cache and an etag, leg 2 still returns 304 on that etag, and leg 3 still returns 200 with a full body and an etag differing from the stale tag supplied. The test case holding all three legs PASSED under the injected constant, verbatim from the run: 'ok - serves /sc-kit.css as text/css'.
findings.mechanism: Leg 3 compares the returned tag against the STALE tag the client sent, and a constant tag differs from it. The constant-ETag defect only becomes observable when the tag MATCHES and the bytes have CHANGED, which none of the three legs constructs. The investigation's own returning-browser measurement is the thing that actually discriminates, because there the browser sends back a matching tag across a real deploy.
findings.whatLeg3DoesCatch: A server that 304s on the mere PRESENCE of If-None-Match without comparing the value. That is a real bug class, the leg is kept verbatim, and it is not the one the card names.
findings.resolution: The three legs are kept AND supplemented by two assertions that do fire: six assets must yield six distinct validators (kills a constant tag), and a file whose bytes change mid-process must stop 304ing its old validator (kills a startup-computed tag, which the distinctness check alone would pass). A third assertion, one file on two routes yielding ONE validator, kills a path-derived tag that would otherwise look content-derived.
findings.recommendation: The WDLL item 8 check line should gain a fourth leg for the deployed probe: change one asset, deploy, and re-request with the etag captured BEFORE the deploy. It must return 200 with a new validator. That is the deployed equivalent of the mid-process test and it is the leg that actually catches the named defect.
findings.processNote: DEV_PROCESS 3.2 -- a brief's numbers are the planner's and reporting one as wrong is a successful outcome. 3.2a -- this correction quotes the source text and names its evidence.

findings.title: If-None-Match: * now returns 304 where it returned 200.
findings.detail: Correct per RFC 9110: '*' matches any existing representation. The investigation used it as its strongest before-state probe and recorded a 200. Asserted in the new RFC-forms test so it cannot regress unnoticed.
findings.consequence: Any future before/after comparison that reuses '*' as a 'this cannot possibly 304' control must be re-based; that control is now expected to 304.

findings.severity: note for the deploy leg, not a defect here
findings.title: The measurement's honest limits carry forward.
findings.detail: The investigation measured Chrome and Chromium only; Firefox and Safari were not measured, and no intermediary proxy was in the path. no-cache plus a strong validator is the header set that makes a city-IT proxy applying a default TTL to a validator-less 200 a non-issue, so this fix narrows that unquantified risk rather than depending on it being absent.
